subject: general
question: Where should the object be placed around the concave mirror to ensure that the size of the image is the same as the size of the object?

options.text: Between focus F and centre of curvature C
Between focus F and pole P

solution:
The correct answer is __**At C, centre of curvature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object is placed **at the centre of curvature (C)** of a concave mirror, the image formed is of the **same size** as the object.
 
• The **image** formed in this case is **real, inverted**, and located at the centre of curvature itself (C).
 
• This happens because at the centre of curvature, the object and its image are equidistant from the mirror, and the curvature of the mirror ensures that light rays converge perfectly to form an image of the same size.
 
• The **laws of reflection** explain this phenomenon, where the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
 
• This property of concave mirrors is used in various **optical instruments** like reflecting telescopes and shaving mirrors where magnification or clarity is required at specific distances.
 
• For practical purposes, this placement is crucial in understanding the behavior of light and the principles of image formation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Between focus F and centre of curvature C**__

 __
 
• When the object is placed between the **focus (F)** and the **centre of curvature (C)**, the image formed is **real, inverted**, and **larger than the object**.
 
• This is a characteristic property of concave mirrors where magnification increases as the object approaches the focus.
 
 
 
• **At focus F**__
 __
 
• When the object is placed at the **focus (F)**, the reflected rays become **parallel**, and the image is formed at **infinity**.
 
• The image in this case is highly magnified, real, and inverted.
 
 
 
• **Between focus F and pole P**__
 
 
• If the object is placed between the **focus (F)** and the **pole (P)**, the image formed is **virtual, erect**, and **magnified**.
 
• This property is used in applications such as **makeup mirrors** or **dentist’s mirrors**.
